title: Merck & Co Inc: A Significant Addition to Eaton Vance Worldwide Health Sciences Fund
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Exploring the Fund's Strategic Moves in the Healthcare Sector

Eaton Vance Worldwide Health Sciences Fund (Trades, Portfolio) recently submitted its N-PORT filing for the first quarter of 2026, revealing strategic investment decisions. The fund, based in Boston and London, focuses on companies engaged in healthcare advancements, including biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medical equipment. With an emphasis on growth driven by aging demographics, innovation, and rising global incomes, the fund aims to capitalize on increasing healthcare spending. The portfolio managers prioritize stocks that are reasonably priced relative to their fundamental value, with potential for long-term growth. Their stock selection process considers factors like market share potential for larger companies and research and development prospects for smaller ones.

The second largest increase was in UnitedHealth Group Inc (NYSE:UNH), with an additional 18,123 shares, bringing the total to 109,349. This adjustment represents a 19.87% increase in share count, with a total value of $32,068,780.

Summary of Sold Out

Eaton Vance Worldwide Health Sciences Fund (Trades, Portfolio) completely exited five holdings in the first quarter of 2026. Notable exits include IDEXX Laboratories Inc (NASDAQ:IDXX), with the sale of all 14,478 shares, resulting in a -1.24% impact on the portfolio. title: Apogee Therapeutics (APGE) Is Up 17.8% After $403 Million Follow-On Tied To Zumilokibart Data
content:
Apogee Therapeutics recently completed a follow-on equity offering of approximately US$403,000,000, issuing 5,750,000 common shares at US$70.00 each after reporting positive 52-week Phase 2 APEX data for its lead atopic dermatitis drug candidate, zumilokibart. The Phase 2 results highlighted zumilokibart’s durable responses with less frequent 3- and 6-month maintenance dosing, while the fresh capital bolsters Apogee’s ability to fund later-stage clinical development. For Apogee, being a shareholder really comes down to believing that zumilokibart can convert its promising Phase 2 profile into a meaningful atopic dermatitis franchise, while the rest of the immunology pipeline adds follow-on value over time. The latest 52-week APEX data meaningfully sharpen that story by reinforcing less frequent dosing as a potential differentiator, which now looks like one of the key near-term catalysts alongside the upcoming APEX Part B readout and any Phase 3 design clarity. title: Apogee CEO Sells 20,000 Shares as Stock Surges Nearly 100% in a Year, but Here's What Really Matters for Investors
content:
Michael Thomas Henderson, Chief Executive Officer of Apogee Therapeutics(NASDAQ:APGE), reported the sale of 20,000 shares of common stock in multiple open-market transactions on March 11, 2026, according to a SEC Form 4 filing.

Transaction summary

Metric Value Shares sold (direct) 20,000 Transaction value $1.5 million Post-transaction common shares (direct) 1,152,987 Post-transaction value (direct ownership) ~$86.11 million

Transaction value based on SEC Form 4 weighted average purchase price ($74.78).

Key questions

How does this sale compare to Henderson's historical trading activity?
This 20,000-share sale matches the median size of his recent sell-only transactions (20,000 shares), consistent with his pattern of periodic, similarly sized disposals since January 2025. What proportion of Henderson's direct equity stake was affected?
The sale accounted for 1.71% of his direct holdings at the time, a level in line with the recent median percentage of holdings per sale (1.62%) and below the higher median from earlier periods (1.91%). Were any shares sold indirectly or through derivative mechanisms?
No; all shares in this transaction were held and sold directly, with no involvement of trusts, entities, or derivative securities. Does this activity materially impact Henderson's remaining stake or align with company performance?
Henderson retains a large direct position (~1.15 million shares, valued at ~$86.11 million).

Company overview

Metric Value Price (as of Thursday) $79.46 Market capitalization $5.5 billion Net income (TTM) -$255.84 million 1-year price change 98%

Company snapshot

Apogee Therapeutics develops biologic therapeutics targeting atopic dermatitis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and related inflammatory and immunology conditions, with lead candidates including APG777 and APG808. The firm operates a biotechnology model focused on advancing proprietary monoclonal antibody programs through clinical development, aiming to generate value through successful trial outcomes, regulatory approvals, and potential partnerships or licensing agreements. It targets patients affected by atopic dermatitis and COPD, with primary customers expected to include healthcare providers, payers, and specialty pharmaceutical distributors upon commercialization.

Apogee Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company specializing in the development of extended half-life monoclonal antibodies for immunological and inflammatory diseases. With a pipeline of differentiated biologics and a focus on subcutaneous delivery, the company seeks to address significant unmet medical needs in dermatology and pulmonology. Apogee's strategy leverages proprietary antibody engineering to achieve competitive advantages in dosing convenience and therapeutic efficacy.

Story Continues

What this transaction means for investors

Thomas’ sale was executed under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, which shifts the focus away from insider sentiment and back toward whether the company’s clinical progress and capital position justify its valuation.

And at Apogee Therapeutics, recent updates point to meaningful forward momentum. The company just reported positive 52-week Phase 2 data for its lead candidate, with up to 85% of patients maintaining key response metrics and evidence of deepening efficacy over time. That durability, paired with less frequent dosing, could position the drug as differentiated in a crowded atopic dermatitis market. Additional readouts are expected in the second quarter, with Phase 3 trials slated to begin in the second half of the year.

Just as importantly, Apogee recently priced a $350 million equity offering that’s expected to close on Thursday, strengthening its balance sheet and extending its runway as it moves into later-stage development. That capital raise suggests management is prioritizing execution over near-term dilution concerns, and investors should stay focused on the results.

title: APGE Stock Up as Skin Disease Drug Shows Sustained 52-Week Efficacy
content:
Shares of Apogee Therapeutics APGE surged 20% on Monday after the company announced positive 52-week maintenance data from Part A of a mid-stage study of zumilokibart (APG777), a potential best-in-class anti-IL-13 antibody, in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD).

Part A of the phase II APEX clinical study enrolled 123 adult patients who were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive zumilokibart or placebo. Patients were given an induction regimen of 720 mg at weeks 0 and 2, followed by 360 mg at weeks 4 and 12. Those who showed clinical benefit continued into the maintenance phase, with assessment of zumilokibart dosing every three or six months.

In 2025, Apogee Therapeutics reported positive top-line data from Part A of the APEX study. At 16 weeks, zumilokibart showed strong efficacy, meeting the primary endpoint with a 71% reduction in Eczema Area Severity Index (EASI) compared with 33.8% for placebo. The candidate had achieved a best-in-class EASI-75 response of 66.9% compared with 24.6% on placebo, with consistent benefits across patients with moderate and severe AD. Outcomes improved with higher exposure levels, with top quartiles reaching EASI-75 rates of 83.3% and 89.5%.

Key secondary endpoints were also favorable, including Validated Investigator’s Global Assessment (vIGA) 0/1 (34.9% vs. 17.3%) and EASI-90 (33.9% vs. 14.7%), while the highest exposure group showed even stronger responses (63.2% for both vIGA 0/1 and EASI-90 at week 16). Zumilokibart also demonstrated rapid itch relief, with statistically significant improvement seen as early as Week 1. The safety profile was favorable and consistent with agents in the class. Adverse events related to treatment were mostly mild to moderate in severity. There were no injection site reactions reported, supporting zumilokibart’s tolerability profile.

APGE’s 52-Week Zumilokibart Maintenance Phase Data in Detail

Apogee Therapeutics reported that 52-week results from the phase II APEX Part A study showed sustained efficacy with both three- and six-month maintenance dosing of zumilokibart. The data also indicated continued improvement over time across lesion and itch measures, including in patients who were not initial responders at 16 weeks. This trend contrasts with existing therapies, where benefits often stabilize earlier, and highlights the candidate’s potential for longer-term disease control with less frequent dosing.

Story Continues

Among the 16-week responders, clinical benefits were largely preserved through 52 weeks. EASI-75 responses were maintained in 75% and 85% of patients on the three and six-month regimens, respectively, while vIGA 0/1 responses remained high at 86% and 78%. Outcomes across key endpoints continued to improve with ongoing treatment, supporting the durability of effect across both dosing schedules.

Beyond the responder subset, the broader study population also demonstrated incremental gains through 52 weeks, suggesting that extended therapy may enhance outcomes even in slower responders. This reinforces the consistency of treatment benefit across patient groups and time.

Zumilokibart was generally well-tolerated over 52 weeks, with a consistent safety profile. Overall, the combination of durable efficacy, deepening responses and the potential for as few as two to four dosing days per year underscores zumilokibart’s promise as a convenient, long-acting therapy for AD.

In the same press release, Apogee Therapeutics stated that Part B of the APEX study is currently underway. This dose-optimization portion of the mid-stage study has enrolled 347 patients, randomized equally to receive zumilokibart (high, medium, and low doses) or placebo. Topline 16-week results from Part B are expected in the second quarter of 2026. Based on the current findings and the anticipated Part B data, and subject to clinical and regulatory outcomes, APGE intends to initiate phase III development of zumilokibart in the second half of 2026, eyeing a potential commercial launch in 2029.
